scenes.headline: How a pointer head speeds up a speedrun
scenes.sub: Copying earlier tokens, mixed into the output distribution.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mousse! Today: how one small pointer head took eleven percent off the fastest recipe for training a small language model.

scenes.text: Let the model point at a token it already read in this document, instead of re-encoding it through the vocabulary softmax.
scenes.mark: point at a token it already read
scenes.say: The idea is old. When the next token already appeared in the document, point at it instead of producing it from scratch.

scenes.title: Two ways to say a name again

left.title: Vocabulary softmax
items: Carry the token in the residual stream
left.say: A normal model has to carry the name forward, then pick it again out of fifty thousand tokens.

right.title: Pointer
items: Attend back to where it was
right.say: A pointer only has to find where the name was, and copy whatever sits there.

steps.say: The last hidden state feeds the usual vocabulary softmax. One spare padding row becomes a copy slot, and its probability is the gate.
The same state feeds a pointer head. It attends back over earlier tokens of the same document, plus a learned sink.
Attention on a matching earlier token becomes copy probability. Attention on the sink goes back to the language model.
The gate mixes the two into one distribution that still sums to one.

scenes.title: The mixture
scenes.text: p(y) = p_lm(1 - a(1 - sink)) + a p_copy

parts.note: the usual softmax, over the real vocabulary
parts.say: The language model keeps most of the mass.

parts.note: gate times the pointer's mass on y
parts.say: The gate times the pointer's copy probability adds the rest.

parts.note: pointer mass handed back to the LM
parts.say: Whatever the pointer parks on the sink is returned, so a miss costs less.

scenes.title: Same node, runs alternating
scenes.say: Each step costs about one percent more. But the run needs a hundred and forty-four fewer steps, and the time falls by eleven percent.

steps.say: The authors plot every record's speedup against the parameters it added.
The star adds almost no parameters, and no big table of memorized n-grams.

scenes.text: A pointer copies from the document cheaply: it does not re-encode the token, it only finds where it was.
scenes.mark: it only finds where it was
scenes.say: So the lesson: a pointer never rebuilds a token it already read. It just finds where it was.

recap: A spare vocab row as the gate
scenes.say: A pointer, a gate, and fewer steps to the same loss.
